source_title: 0xSero/ascii-art: Dot-lattice art: photo to two-tone dot map to seamless animated loop (engine + scripts) - GitHub
source_excerpt:
Turn any photo, sculpture, object or drawing into a figure made of dots on a fixed grid — charcoal ground, two grey tones, rare crimson — then animate it into a seamless loop: disintegration into wind-blown dust, things emerging or growing out of the figure, voids, tentacles, fine-stipple creatures.
This repo is the skill: the method, the engine, and the scripts that do the mechanical parts.
Python 3.10+ with numpy , scipy , Pillow , scikit-image
playwright with a chromium build ( python -m playwright install chromium )
grab_frames.py out.html sheet.png sheet captures a contact sheet instead of frames.
Coverage matters more than contrast: most subject cells should be bright ; dim dots are shadow accents, empty cells are line art (eyes, mouth, the deepest folds).
SKILL.md — the craft: anatomy, step-by-step method, motion vocabulary, loop maths, review checklist.
references/engine.md — scene JSON format, layers and their parameters.
references/case-study.md — one piece end to end, including every round of feedback.
examples/scenes/*.json and examples/bust-skull.map.txt are the scenes and dot map of one finished piece. The reference photographs they point at are not included (third-party imagery), so the scenes document structure rather than run as-is; bust-skull.map.txt is enough to build the figure layers.
MIT — see LICENSE . It covers this code and text only. Any image you feed the scripts stays yours (or its owner's); nothing here grants rights to it.
